question.problem:
Upon launching a new online course, the chief financial officer (CFO) of a company estimates that its profit, in thousands of dollars, is given by

$$
P(x)=0.3{x}^{3}-3.6{x}^{2}+10.8x+5,
$$

where $x$ is the price, in dollars, of a single course. If the CFO estimates that the course price should be between $$1$ and $$7,$ at what price is the maximum profit obtained?

The profit is maximum when a single course costs $$$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since $x$ represents the price of a single course and since the CFO estimates that the course price should be between $$1$ and $$7,$  the permitted domain for $x$ is given by

$$
1\le x\le 7.
$$

We need to find the critical points of $P(x)$ for $1<x<7.$ Taking the derivative, we get

$$
{P}^{′}(x)=0.9{x}^{2}-7.2x+10.8.
$$

and solving ${P}^{′}(x)=0$ gives the following critical points:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(x) & =0 \\ 0.9{x}^{2}-7.2x+10.8 & =0 \\ 0.9({x}^{2}-8x+12) & =0 \\ 0.9(x-2)(x-6) & =0 \\ x & =2,6\end{aligned}
$$

All that's left now is to find which of $x=2$ or $x=6$ gives a maximum value of $P(x).$ To do this, we compute the second derivative:

$$
{P}^{″}(x)=1.8x-7.2
$$

Substituting $x=2$ and $x=6$ into ${P}^{″}(x),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{″}(2) & =1.8(2)-7.2=-3.6<0, \\ {P}^{″}(6) & =1.8(6)-7.2=3.6>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the second derivative is negative at $x=2,$ the point $x=2$ is indeed a local maximum of $P(x).$

Our candidates are $x=1,$ $x=2$ and $x=7.$ Computing $P(x)$ at each of these values, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1) & =0.3(1)^{3}-3.6(1)^{2}+10.8(1)+5=12.5 \\ P(2) & =0.3(2)^{3}-3.6(2)^{2}+10.8(2)+5=14.6\,✓ \\ P(7) & =0.3(7)^{3}-3.6(7)^{2}+10.8(7)+5=7.1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=2$ is the global maximum of $P(x).$ So, the profit is maximum when a single course costs $$\,2.$
